dedupe_keys.name: geer southern montana yellowstone flood reconnaissance 2022

description: GEER Southern Montana/Yellowstone Flood Reconnaissance 2022 is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "field recon", published or maintained by Anne Lemnitzer, University of California Irvine (uci.edu). In June 2022, the southern part of Montana and the northern part of Yellowstone National Park experienced flooding along multiple watersheds, including the Yellowstone River. The flooding resulted from heavy snowmelt between June 10-13th, leading to record levels of river water elevation in most of the main tributaries to the Yellowstone River. Coverage: Yellowstone River in Montana and Wyoming. DesignSafe files it as a "field recon" project. Keywords: Yellowstone River, Southern Montana Flooding, Reconnaissance, Geotechnical Damage, Sediment Transport and Redeposition, Infrastructure Damage. Published 2023-06-16. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
